_readme: data/layer-floors.json - the committed ABSOLUTE floors for the prebuilt FlatGeobuf layer
sets, read by scripts/build-manifest.js (Level 1 and Level 2 of the build gates) before the
layers/current.json pointer is written.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. No absolute floor in this pipeline is ever a continental measurement.
A floor whose basis is a different bounding box than the published mask is not a floor: it is
either a day-one hard refusal that makes the pipeline unpublishable, or a number the interior
surplus clears while every Great Lakes shoreline beach is missing. So every floor here is
SEEDED FROM A REAL BUILD UNDER THE PUBLISHED MASK, cross-checked by a human against D1 truth,
and moved only by a reviewed commit - exactly the discipline data/marine-zones-greatlakes.json
already has.
WHY IT IS KEYED BY regionsDigest. The digest is sha256 over regionsDigestInput(REGIONS) from
src/layerManifest.js: region name plus bbox, sorted, canonical JSON. Appending a coastal box
to src/regions.js changes the digest, so the new footprint has NO entry here and the build
REFUSES to auto-publish until someone seeds and commits floors for it. That is what turns
"remember to add a coastline floor when the first saltwater box lands" from prose into a
build-time refusal - without it, a Pacific box would silently mass-hide every ocean beach.
HOW TO SEED A NEW DIGEST.
1. Run build-layers.yml by workflow_dispatch with publish true (bootstrap: the ratio checks
have no previous manifest to run against, so the pointer is not written automatically).
2. Read the produced manifest.json. Confirm lakes-polygon is exactly 6 features carrying
exactly the six wikidata QIDs in lakesIdentity below, and cross-check the global and
per-region counts against D1 truth before trusting any of them.
3. Commit an entry under the new digest with status "seeded", seededFromBuildId set to that
manifest buildId, and each floor set to 0.75x the seeded count (rounded down), EXCEPT the
lakes identity, which is an identity and not a ratio.
SHAPE.
floors[<regionsDigest>].status          "bootstrap" | "seeded"
floors[<regionsDigest>].layers[<key>]   global feature-count floor, keyed by the ten
EXPECTED_LAYER_KEYS of src/layerManifest.js
floors[<regionsDigest>].regions[<name>][<layer>]
per-REGION envelope-intersection floor, keyed by the
src/regions.js REGIONS name and one of the six
LOGICAL layer names listed in _regionLayerNames
lakesIdentity                           digest-independent identity, not a heuristic
A null floor means NO FLOOR HAS BEEN SEEDED YET and the corresponding Level 1 / Level 2 check
does not apply. A null is deliberate and reviewable; an invented number is not. A floors file
carrying made-up counts is strictly worse than one carrying nulls, because a wrong floor either
blocks every build forever or blesses a broken one.
status "bootstrap" is NOT a licence to auto-publish. An entry whose status is "bootstrap"
records that the footprint is known and its floors are still pending; the pointer step must
still require an explicit workflow_dispatch with publish true. Only status "seeded" (with the
nulls replaced by real, reviewed numbers) means the digest is fully gated. Do not add a
bootstrap entry for a NEW footprint just to get past a refusal - that defeats the entire
purpose of keying this file by digest.

_comment: The ONLY hardcoded absolute in the whole gate set, and the sharpest canary in it: the six
Great Lake relations are the largest and most reference-heavy objects in the data, so if the
GDAL node index broke, lakes-polygon.fgb goes empty first. This is an IDENTITY - exactly six
features carrying exactly these six QIDs - not a floor, so it never moves with the mask and
is not nested under a digest. build-manifest.js should assert it against GREAT_LAKE_QIDS in
src/waterClass.js (the set src/waterClass.js actually classifies with) rather than trusting
this file alone; the copy here exists so the expected values are readable next to the floors.
BOOTSTRAP ENTRY for the Great Lakes footprint - the nine REGIONS boxes of src/regions.js as
of the FlatGeobuf migration. Every floor below is null because build 1 has not run: build 1 is
what SEEDS these numbers, under the published mask, and a human commits them here afterwards
(see _readme, HOW TO SEED A NEW DIGEST). Until then no absolute or per-region floor applies
and the layers/current.json pointer must be written only by an explicit workflow_dispatch.
The digest key was computed as sha256 over regionsDigestInput(REGIONS) from
src/layerManifest.js. VERIFY IT against the regionsDigest the first manifest actually carries
before seeding: if the two disagree the build refuses to auto-publish, which is the safe
direction, but the fix is to correct this key rather than to loosen the check.
coastline is legitimately null-and-zero at Great Lakes scope: the lakes are mapped as water
relations, not natural=coastline ways, which is why 100% of the served Great Lakes rows
classify through the wikidata QID path. It becomes structurally REQUIRED the moment a
saltwater box lands - and that box changes the digest, so it needs a fresh entry anyway.
parks-line has one extra rule that is not a ratio: a count of ZERO is a hard REFUSAL even
while the floor here is null. Named park ways exist unconditionally in this scope, so zero
means the carve is broken, and the visible consequence is unnamed beaches plus DELETED
park-origin rows - which is the majority of the table (982 of 1669 rows are park-origin).
regionNames: Lake St. Clair + St. Clair / Detroit Rivers
